transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Jordan Kim (Redwood Product), Rohit Sharma (VeloxSearch Head of Search), Maya Lopez (Eng Manager), Samir Patel (ML Engineer)

Auto-generated summary: quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + reranking endpoints, discussed baseline pipeline, integration options, security/compliance questions, agreed to run a pilot benchmark for 1k queries.

00:00 Alicia Park: hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate you taking the time. quick intros?
00:08 Rohit Sharma: yeah thanks, rohit here, head of search at veloxsearch. we're looking at vector-based rerank to improve our query relevance for product search.
00:15 Maya Lopez: maya, engineering manager on search infra. mainly interested in latency and cost impact.
00:20 Samir Patel: samir, ml engineer, i'll be running tests and integrating.
00:24 Alicia Park: great. marcus i'll hand to you for a quick product walkthrough - embeddings + rerank on the hosted API side.
00:30 Marcus Li: awesome, thanks alicia. ok so at a high level, redwood hosted api gives you two primitives that we usually combine - embeddings endpoint and a rerank endpoint, or you can do a similarity search client-side and call the generation model for reordering. today i'll focus on embeddings + rerank flow that we demo in our search reference app.
00:55 Marcus Li: first step is embedding your corpus, we support dense vector endpoints with incremental upserts, you can stream or batch. there's a simple /v1/embeddings call and we return 1536-d vectors for the default model or 1024 depending on model choice - sorry some models vary.
01:12 Samir Patel: are we locked to a specific dims size? our index is currently 768 dim with faiss.
01:18 Marcus Li: good q - you can project, but typically teams either reindex to new dims or use a packing layer. we also provide pre-quantized embeddings, and we have tooling in the console to preview dimension mismatches.
01:35 Rohit Sharma: what's your latency for a single embedding call and bulk upsert?
01:40 Marcus Li: single call avg for the smaller models is ~60-120ms, larger ones 200-400ms. for bulk upserts we recommend chunked uploads and our dedicated autoscale handles throughput; expect a near-linear throughput with small batching.
01:55 Maya Lopez: and storage/retention? we have PII concerns and our legal is asking about data persistence.
02:01 Alicia Park: we have retention controls on the hosted API, plus customer data segregation; for regulated data you can opt for private deployment - but hosted supports configurable retention and delete-by-query endpoints. we also integrate with KMS for encryption at rest.
02:18 Rohit Sharma: ok good. show us the rerank flow.
02:22 Marcus Li: right - rerank endpoint is basically a lightweight model that takes original query + candidate doc snippets + embeddings and produces a reorder score or direct reranked list. there is a dedicated /v1/rerank endpoint and we also have a guided prompt variant for more explainable signals.
02:40 Marcus Li: the common pattern: run a kNN on your vector store to get top N candidates, then call /v1/rerank with up to 40 candidates per request, send the query and the candidate contexts. we return scores and an ordered list.
02:56 Samir Patel: 40 candidates, is that a hard limit? we sometimes pull 100.
03:01 Marcus Li: right now we recommend keeping it under 50 for latency reasons; you can chunk, but each chunk is an additional model call. for larger candidate sets, we suggest cascade - coarse vector similarity then lightweight transform reranker.
03:15 Rohit Sharma: what's the per-request cost profile? we're trying to estimate unit economics.
03:20 Marcus Li: cost depends on model choice and candidate count. rough example: embeddings $0.0004 per embed, rerank lightweight model $0.001 per call for up to 10 candidates, scales linearly. we'll send a pricing sheet with sample scenarios - marcus: can you note to run a cost sim for their 1k queries?
03:34 Marcus Li: yep noted.
03:36 Jordan Kim: also in Redwood Optimize we have a batching/caching suggester that looks at your query distribution and recommends prefix caching + batch sizes to hit your latency SLO vs cost target.
03:48 Maya Lopez: curious about SLO - our p95 target is 120ms from user - how realistic is that with hosted?
03:54 Marcus Li: for pure embedding + vector lookup, it's doable, but with rerank step it depends - you can often keep p95 under 200ms with smaller candidate sets and aggressive batching. many customers do hybrid: do vector nearest neighbors in their infra and call Redwood for rerank only which helps.
04:12 Rohit Sharma: hmm our current pipeline keeps everything in-house because of concerns about data residency and also we run at high qps during peak.
04:20 Alicia Park: totally fair - can I ask about your schedule and stakeholders? are you evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private?
04:27 Rohit Sharma: we're primarily evaluating hosted for quickest time to market, but dedicated or private is on the table if the economics and compliance line up. procurement will likely push dedicated for workload isolation.
04:40 Samir Patel: one more technical - how does Redwood handle KV cache and multi-turn state? we have conversational signals in product search.
04:47 Marcus Li: sorry i said KV cache earlier - that's more for generation performance; for rerank we support including session context as part of the input. we do maintain tokenized context handling and a small short-term cache on the serving side to speed consecutive similar calls. sometimes transcripts say k-v cache but it's more like prefix cache.
05:05 Maya Lopez: can you show the console demo?
05:08 Marcus Li: sure, i'm going to share the console link - (link) - apologies the auto-transcript sometimes garbles URLs.
05:15
05:15 Marcus Li: ok in the console you can: upload datasets, preview embeddings, run a sample rerank, and check per-route latency/cost breakdowns. here's a quick run: i'll paste a query and 6 candidate docs and call the rerank endpoint.
05:30
05:30 [demonstration noise, typing sounds]
06:00 Marcus Li: all right results returned - you can see scores and confidence signals, also a debug view that shows token-level attention highlights (approximate). note these are illustrative.
06:15 Samir Patel: looks promising. is the debug view available in hosted or only in dedicated?
06:21 Marcus Li: available in hosted but redacted in some compliance tiers; for enterprise we can provide richer logging in dedicated/private with audit controls.
06:32 Rohit Sharma: security: SOC 2, SSO, SAML, audit logs - do you have those docs?
06:38 Alicia Park: yes we do. i'll drop the SOC 2 and security pack link after the call; we also support SAML SSO, RBAC, and can integrate with your KMS for key management.
06:50 Rohit Sharma: and data residency - can we lock data to eu-west or us-east?
06:54 Alicia Park: hosted supports region pinning for data storage and processing in major regions; for strict residency we often recommend Private. we'll surface region options in the pricing sheet.
07:06 Maya Lopez: curious about fallback behavior - what happens when capacity is constrained?
07:10 Marcus Li: smart routing: requests can route to cheaper/compatible model variants or fallback to a smaller model; for critical queries you can enable automatic fallback policies. there's also canary and rollout controls in console.
07:23 Rohit Sharma: latency degradation during peak is our main fear - can we run a benchmark?
07:27 Alicia Park: yes that was our main ask too - marcus will run a 1,000 query rerank test with their query log sample; results will include p50/p95, token counts, and cost per 1k.
07:40 Marcus Li: i'll do that, and i'll include a couple of model variants and batch configs.
07:44 Samir Patel: integration work - do you have SDKs or open-source clients? we use python and go.
07:49 Marcus Li: SDKs for python, node, and go; plus cURL examples. integration is simply call embeddings upsert route and rerank route. we also have a quickstart repo.
07:58 Rohit Sharma: any customers in the e-commerce space you can share?
08:01 Alicia Park: yes a few anonymized case studies - i'll send links.
08:06 Maya Lopez: timeline: if we want to pilot in jan/feb, what's needed?
08:10 Alicia Park: we'll need sample logs, target KPIs, and a PO/statement so we can spin up trial quota. pilot generally 2-4 weeks for the rerank bench.
08:20 Rohit Sharma: sounds good. question from legal - do you provide DPA and standard contract templates?
08:25 Alicia Park: yes, we'll include DPA and standard terms with the pilot paperwork.
08:30
08:30 [brief crosstalk]
08:35 Marcus Li: quick note on cost optimizations - quantized embeddings and using a smaller reranker as a filter stage can reduce cost 2-3x. Optimize will analyze and recommend these changes for their distribution.
08:50 Samir Patel: do you do on-prem model hosting for private? some of our customers require air-gapped verification.
08:56 Alicia Park: we offer Private with an on-prem package; audit logs and HSM integrations included. that's usually a later phase.
09:05 Rohit Sharma: ok let's recap next steps.
09:08 Alicia Park: recap: 1) Marcus to run 1k-query rerank benchmark with our model variants and share spreadsheet by jan 5. 2) Alicia to send pricing, SOC 2/security pack, DPA, and pilot contract by dec 24. 3) Rohit to share sample query logs and relevancy KPIs by dec 29. 4) schedule a follow-up in early jan to review results.
09:40 Rohit Sharma: yep we're aligned. thanks everyone.
09:44 Maya Lopez: thanks all.
09:46 Alicia Park: thank you, we'll follow up with links. talk soon.
